scenario.name: CISA & Microsoft DFIR — Volume Shadow Copy & esentutl.exe NTDS.dit Extraction Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a bank whose master account ledger stays bolted down to the vault floor while the bank is open so nobody can walk out with it. An intruder snaps a frozen carbon-copy photograph of the entire floor, uses the bank own official bookbinding copier to stream the ledger cleanly out of the frozen photograph, and separately steals the four-part decoder dial from the wall safe so they can read every password seal offline. In this scenario (T1003.003, CISA & Microsoft DFIR, Volume Shadow Copy & esentutl.exe NTDS.dit Extraction Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: volume Shadow Copy Creation via vssadmin.exe, then eSENT Database Streaming via esentutl.exe /y, then sYSTEM Registry Hive BootKey Extraction. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Volume Shadow Copy Creation via vssadmin.exe, then ESENT Database Streaming via esentutl.exe /y, then SYSTEM Registry Hive BootKey Extraction, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.003 - OS Credential Dumping: NTDS)
stages.description:
Unable to pry the live master ledger off the vault desk while clerks are using it, the intruder activates the building built-in instant camera to capture a frozen read-only snapshot of the entire drive floor. Because the Active Directory Extensible Storage Engine database (C:\Windows\NTDS
tds.dit) is exclusively locked by lsass.exe while the Domain Controller is running, the attacker spawns vssadmin.exe create shadow /for=C: to instruct the Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) to snapshot the C: volume into \?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy1 (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon / 7036 , System SCM, Image=C:\Windows\System32\vssadmin.exe, ShadowVolume=\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy1, TargetDatabase=C:\Windows\NTDS
tds.dit so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes vssadmin.exe create shadow /for=C: (which invokes the Volume Shadow Copy Service administration CLI , vssadmin.exe create shadow /for=C: to instruct vssvc.exe and volsnap.sys to freeze a re so that bypasses the exclusive kernel file lock held by lsass.exe/NTDS on C:\Windows\NTDS
tds.dit and HKLM\SYSTEM , T1003.003, allowing the attacker to copy the Active Directory password database from the unlocked shadow volume). Next, the follow-up artifact sc.exe query vss # System EventID 7036: Volume Shadow Copy service entered the running state runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , sc.exe query vss # System EventID 7036: Volume Shadow Copy service entered the running state so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.003 during "Volume Shadow Copy Creation via vssadmin.exe & vssvc.exe , EventID 1 & 7036" , Because the Active Directory Extensible Storage Engine database , C:\Windows\NTDS
tds while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: ESENT Database Streaming via esentutl.exe /y /vss (Application ESENT EventID 325 & 326)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.003 - ESENT EventID 325/326 Artifact)
stages.description:
Stepping up to the frozen floor photograph, the intruder calls over the bank own signed book-repair utility to peel a clean copy of the master ledger right out of the snapshot while the database engine quietly stamps an internal audit ticket. The attacker invokes the signed Microsoft Extensible Storage Engine utility (esentutl.exe /y /vss C:\Windows\NTDS
tds.dit /d C:\Temp
tds.dit) or ntdsutil.exe "ac i ntds" "ifm". Even if command-line logs are evaded, the Windows Application log records ESENT EventID 325 (New database created: C:\Temp
tds.dit) and EventID 326/327 (Database engine attached/detached) (logged in WinEvent Event 325 with Provider=ESENT , Application Event Log, EventID=325 , Database Created / 326 , Database Attached, SourceDatabase=C:\Windows\NTDS
tds.dit, StagedDatabasePath=C:\Windows\Temp
tds.dit so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes esentutl.exe /y /vss C:\Windows\NTDS
tds.dit /d C:\Windows\Temp
tds.dit (which executes Microsoft's signed Extensible Storage Engine utility , esentutl.exe with the /y , file copy and /vss , Volume Shadow Copy switches to stre so that performs Living-off-the-Land credential database extraction , T1003.003 during "ESENT Database Streaming via esentutl.exe /y /vss , Application ESENT EventID 325 & 326" using a trusted Microsoft binary in C:\Windows\System32, while inadvertently generating deterministic ESENT EventID 325/326 telemetry in the Windows Application log). Next, the follow-up artifact ntdsutil.exe "ac i ntds" "ifm" "create full C:\Windows\Temp\IFM" q q runs (which Runs the native Active Directory maintenance CLI , ntdsutil.exe with chained interactive subcommands , "ac i ntds" -> activate instance ntds, "ifm" so that extracts every domain user, administrator, and krbtgt password hash in a single signed utility invocation , T1003.003 during "ESENT Database Streaming via esentutl.exe /y /vss , Application ESENT EventID 325 & 326" so the attacker can crack hashes or forge Golden Tickets offline). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ esentutl.exe /y /vss C:\Windows\NTDS
tds.dit /d C:\Windows\Temp
tds.dit / ⇠#2 ACK 325) from Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch) to Node ③ (#3 Core DC VLAN Switch (:445)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 NTDS.dit & SYSTEM Hive Store).

stages.title: Stage 3: SYSTEM Registry Hive BootKey Extraction (reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM) & Offline SecretsDump
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.002 - Security Account Manager / SYSTEM BootKey)
stages.description: Because every password line inside the stolen ledger is scrambled by a secret master cipher wheel bolted inside the wall cabinet, the intruder also exports that entire system cabinet so they can unwind every employee secret offline without touching the bank again. Because ntds.dit PekList password hashes are encrypted with the Domain Controller BootKey stored across four scrambled registry keys (JD, Skew1, GBG, Data under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa), the attacker runs reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\sys.hiv and exfiltrates both files to run Impacket secretsdump.py offline (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with EventID=11 , Sysmon FileCreate / 4688 , Security, Image=C:\Windows\System32\reg.exe, TargetFilename=C:\Windows\Temp\sys.hiv, ForensicImpact=Offline decryption of all AD user & krbtgt NTLM/AES keys so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\sys.hiv /y (which executes reg.exe save to serialize an active kernel-mounted Windows Registry hive , such as HKLM\SYSTEM, HKLM\SAM, or HKLM\SECURITY into a portable so that extracts the 16-byte SysKey / BootKey , stored across the JD, Skew1, GBG, and Data registry classes under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa required to decrypt the PEK and password hashes inside ntds.dit or SAM , T1003.002). Next, the follow-up artifact vssadmin.exe delete shadows /for=C: /quiet runs (which executes vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet , or WMI Win32_ShadowCopy.Delete to invoke IVssBackupComponents::DeleteSnapshots and purge all exi so that inhibits system recovery , T1003.002 during "SYSTEM Registry Hive BootKey Extraction , reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM & Offline SecretsDump" by destroying local disk shadow copies before or after payload execution so defenders cannot roll back encrypted files or inspect historical volume state). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\sys.hiv /y / ⇠#3 ACK 11) from Node ③ (#3 Core DC VLAN Switch (:445)) to Node ④ (#4 CORP-DC01 (vssvc & esentutl)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 NTDS.dit & SYSTEM Hive Store).

keySpecs.value: Monitor Sysmon EventID 11 (FileCreate) and EventID 13 (RegistryEvent) alongside command-line invocations of reg.exe save targeting HKLM\SYSTEM or HKLM\SAM.

steps.simpleExplanation: Because ntds.dit PekList password hashes are encrypted with the Domain Controller BootKey stored across four scrambled registry keys (JD, Skew1, GBG, Data under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa), the attacker runs reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\sys.hiv and exfiltrates both files to run Impacket secretsdump.py offline (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with EventID=11 , Sysmon FileCreate / 4688 , Security, Image=C:\Windows\System32\reg.exe, TargetFilename=C:\Windows\Temp\sys.hiv, ForensicImpact=Offline decryption of all AD user & krbtgt NTLM/AES keys so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\sys.hiv /y (which executes reg.exe save to serialize an active kernel-mounted Windows Registry hive , such as HKLM\SYSTEM, HKLM\SAM, or HKLM\SECURITY into a portable so that extracts the 16-byte SysKey / BootKey , stored across the JD, Skew1, GBG, and Data registry classes under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa required to decrypt the PEK and password hashes inside ntds.dit or SAM , T1003.002). Next, the follow-up artifact vssadmin.exe delete shadows /for=C: /quiet runs (which executes vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet , or WMI Win32_ShadowCopy.Delete to invoke IVssBackupComponents::DeleteSnapshots and purge all exi so that inhibits system recovery , T1003.002 during "SYSTEM Registry Hive BootKey Extraction , reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM & Offline SecretsDump" by destroying local disk shadow copies before or after payload execution so defenders cannot roll back encrypted files or inspect historical volume state).
